sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Fayetteville
sections.html:
If you are selling a house in Fayetteville, the office to know is Cumberland Tax Administration, which belongs to the county. It sets the value, sends the statement and collects payment. The city levies its own rate, yet both levies print together on the county's single bill.

Visit 117 Dick Street, Room 530, Fayetteville, NC 28301, or phone 910-678-7507. Letters should be addressed to Cumberland Tax Administration, PO Box 449, Fayetteville NC 28302. City rate, county rate and any city fees all sit on one statement. Because of that, a closing agent will ask for your parcel number before quoting a payoff, so have it handy.

sections.h2: Rates and fees on the bill
sections.html:
Two rates and a handful of flat fees make up the bill: 49.9 cents per $100 of value for the county, 44.95 cents per $100 for the city, and set charges for trash and stormwater. The county's rate page covers the 2026 tax bills (fiscal year 2027) and prints each levy as a decimal, with 0.9485 as the combined city figure. A house just outside the city line is billed a different mix, which includes a fire district charge and a recreation rate.

Levies on Fayetteville 2026 tax bills
LevyAmount
County ad valorem rate0.499
City of Fayetteville rate0.4495
Combined city and county rate0.9485
Fayetteville Revitalization District0.1489 + 0.4495, combined 1.0974
City solid waste fee, residential units with seven or fewer units$285 a year
City residential stormwater fee$84, $168 or $252 a year by impervious area tier
City vehicle fee and transit tax$25 and $5 per registered vehicle

Impervious surface decides the stormwater tier: tier 1 is under 2,500 square feet, tier 2 covers 2,501 to 4,800 square feet, and tier 3 is larger than that.

  • Stormwater, solid waste, refuse, recycling and transit charges sit outside the combined rate, so your real total runs higher.
  • A parcel inside the revitalization district pays an extra levy beyond the city rate.

The bill is dated for September 1. Nothing extra accrues until January 6, so January 5 is your real deadline.

These dates come from G.S. 105-360, which applies everywhere in the state. Money received before January 6 settles the bill at face value. On January 6 the balance picks up 2 percent for the rest of January, and every month or partial month beyond that adds three-fourths of one percent. Owners who need to split the bill can call 910-678-7507 and ask about installments.

If you sell, ask the closing attorney to check that the payoff covers this year's bill. Recording a deed does not erase unpaid tax. The lien belongs to the land and travels to the buyer. See G.S. 105-355 for how the lien works.

Cumberland reappraised every parcel at its January 1, 2025 market value, replacing the 2017 figures. The eight year ceiling between reappraisals is a state rule. County staff describe the purpose as fairness among properties rather than a larger or smaller total levy. Rates for the new values began July 1, 2025.

If you already hold an approved relief application, you keep it and do not refile. The exemption itself continues, though the dollar amount on your bill moves with the new value.

sections.h2: Where do I send a challenge to my Fayetteville value?
sections.html:
Begin with an informal Request for Review sent to Tax Administration. A dispute that survives that step moves to the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Informal review: the request can be filed online, mailed, emailed, handed in at Room 530 of the county courthouse (117 Dick Street) or left in the secure drop box in the back lot. Attach recent comparable sales or other proof of value.
  • Deadline: informal appeals for the 2027 tax year are due February 5, 2027, and you should expect a decision letter around April 2027.
  • Board hearing: if the informal stage does not settle it, take the case to the Board of Equalization and Review. Call the office for this year's adjournment date.
  • Further appeal: send written notice to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290).

For a mailed request, address it to Attn: Real Estate Assessment at the PO Box above. List a phone number and mailing address that work, since an appraiser may arrange to visit the house. If you sell before the review ends, tell the office so the letter reaches the right person.

A homeowner picks among three state programs and gets only one: the senior or disability exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, or the circuit breaker cap. Check these before you list, since each changes what the county will say is owed at transfer.

  • Elderly or disabled owners whose 2026 income is $38,800 or below can exclude $25,000 of value, or half of it when half is the bigger number (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • The disabled veteran exclusion removes $45,000 from the taxed value and ignores age and income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Under the circuit breaker, the bill is limited to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent where income falls between $38,800 and $58,200. Whatever exceeds the cap is deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor. January is best, and June 1 before the tax year is the last day. Selling ends a circuit breaker deferral and brings three years of deferred tax due at once, so get that number from the county before you take an offer.

Back taxes come out of your proceeds at the closing table. The lien attached to the parcel on January 1, the listing date, so the buyer's lender will want it cleared.

  1. Ask the county for a written payoff that adds in interest and city fees.
  2. Hand it to your closing attorney well ahead of the signing appointment.
  3. Find out if a circuit breaker deferral is attached to the parcel.
  4. Let the attorney pay the county from your proceeds.
  5. Keep the paid receipt with your closing papers.

Once January 5 passes with the bill open, the county may sue to foreclose its lien. Selling the house first is the simplest cure, since the payoff comes out of the price. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 ends with an auction at the courthouse door. An owner who redeems before the sale is confirmed pays the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

Fayetteville is a renter-heavy market: 47.4 percent of homes are owner occupied (2020 to 2024), and the median value of those homes is $188,000. Median gross rent is $1,250. Many sellers here are landlords, and a rented house is liened just like an owner's home. A cash buyer still sees the same payoff.

A short folder saves days at closing. Pull together your parcel number, your most recent statement from Cumberland Tax Administration, and any approval letter for a relief program you use. If you filed an informal review that is still open, add that paperwork too.

Then call 910-678-7507 and ask what the payoff would be on a given date. Interest and city fees change the figure from week to week, so request it close to your signing day and ask for it in writing. Your closing attorney needs that sheet to wire the county its share, and the title company will hold up the deed until the tax lien is accounted for.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Fayetteville tax statement?
faqs.a: Call Cumberland County Tax Administration at 910-678-7507, or go to Room 530 at 117 Dick Street. Values, bills and payment plans all run through that one desk.

faqs.q: What day does interest start on a Fayetteville bill?
faqs.a: January 6. Pay by January 5 to avoid it. Then 2 percent applies through February 1, and each later month adds three-fourths of one percent.

faqs.q: What combined rate applies inside Fayetteville city limits?
faqs.a: 0.9485 for 2026, which is 0.4495 from the city plus 0.499 from the county. Trash, stormwater and vehicle charges come on top.

faqs.q: Is there still time to appeal a Fayetteville assessment?
faqs.a: For the 2027 tax year, informal requests are due February 5, 2027. Formal appeals follow at the Board of Equalization and Review.

faqs.q: If I sell with tax unpaid, does the debt go with the house?
faqs.a: It can, since the lien belongs to the land. Most sellers have the closing attorney pay it off at closing so the buyer starts clean.
